items.article: Five literary classics that defy the traditional adaptation treatment. These are uniquely suited to the literary medium for good reason Some literary classics have managed to beat the “unadaptable” curse. Frank Herbert’s Dune is a key example, along with Stanisław Lem’s Solaris and Gabriel García Márquez’s One Hundred Years of Solitude . “If it can be written, or thought, it can be filmed,” said director Stanley Kubrick — a statement that has proven to be true in the hands of competent filmmakers. That said, some classic books should never be turned into films. This has less to do with their “unfilmable” nature. Some stories simply lose their essence as soon as they’re translated to another medium. All prose relies on internal narrative logic, but some use experimental formats or themes that only work well on the page. Take Fyodor Dostoevsky’s White Nights . It's a riveting short story about a young man’s loneliness in Saint Petersburg that loses all of its charm as soon as it’s dramatized. (Many have tried, but none have captured the story's distinct mood.) With that in mind, here are five classic books that should never be adapted into movies. Mark Z. items.article: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team looks into whether clubs get compensated in scenarios where their player gets injured on international duty. Clubs whose players suffer injuries on international duty are awarded compensation by Fifa in certain circumstances. Bruno Fernandes, Cody Gakpo, Alexander Isak, Nico O'Reilly, Kai Havertz, Brian Brobbey and Dan Ballard are among the Premier League players already to have sustained injuries during the extended September/October international break, with two full rounds of fixtures remaining. Real Madrid striker and France captain Kylian Mbappe also sustained an injury in this break. If a player on international duty sustains a new injury that prevents them from taking part in full training or matches for a minimum of 28 days, the club they play for will be entitled to financial compensation from the Fifa Club Protection Programme. The compensation package, which is offered based on a player's salary, covers breaks in which international "A" matches are played on the dates of the international match calendar. The eligible period starts from the moment a player leaves their home or parent club's address to attend international duty. It remains until the either midnight local time on the day they return home or 48 hours after leaving their national team, whichever happens first.

The platelet is the smallest component of the human blood—a cell fragment with the primary job of stopping bleeding when injury occurs. When a blood vessel is damaged, platelets cluster together to form a plug, then a clot, to stop blood loss. items.article: After studying stool samples from more than 1,300 cancer patients, scientists uncovered distinct gut microbiome patterns tied to different cancers. Researchers from Mayo Clinic analyzed samples from 1,364 cancer patients across a range of cancer types, stages and treatments as part of the Mayo Clinic Cancer Microbiome Cohort study, published in Cell . Scientists found unique microbiome signatures associated with five major cancer groups, while also identifying notable differences in patients diagnosed at younger ages . One of the most striking findings involved early-onset colorectal and breast cancers , both of which have been increasing among younger adults in recent years. Patients aged 50 and under with colorectal cancer had higher levels of lactate and greater amounts of a bacterium called Veillonella parvula, which feeds on lactate. Meanwhile, younger breast cancer patients showed changes across 64 bacterial species and lower levels of primary bile acids.

Flavor additives commonly found in electronic cigarettes used by millions of Americans can damage joint health – even without any nicotine , according to a study published Wednesday. Cinnamon and menthol flavors proved especially harmful, causing ATDC5 cartilage cells to die, researchers at New Jersey’s Seton Hall University said. And the chemical flavors were also shown to disrupt the cells’ ability to build and maintain healthy tissue, triggering inflammation in the cells and turning on changes in the body that lead to tissue breakdown and cause swelling. "Our findings show that e-cigarette flavor additives are far from benign additives," Jessica Cottrell, an associate professor at the school, said in a statement . "Even without nicotine, these chemical agents alter metabolism, gene expression and inflammatory pathways, which underscores an urgent need to examine how vaping impacts broader musculoskeletal and tissue health."
